implementation_summary: Six review blockers fixed across the A2UI chat surface. FIX-1 (proxy clone): new exported helper `toPlainJson()` in src/a2ui/useA2uiSurface.ts does a JSON round-trip (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))) and replaces both structuredClone() call sites; it reads through the proxy-compare get-traps that structuredClone rejects outright (DataCloneError on any Proxy) and yields plain mutable objects for the SDK DataModel. JSON was chosen over proxy-compare's getUntracked because proxy-compare is only a transitive dependency of valtio (not declared in package.json), and because A2UI envelopes/data models are JSON-by-wire, so the round-trip is lossless. FIX-2 (shallow spread): ChatA2uiBlock no longer does `{...savedDataModel}`; the prefill is serialized as one JSON string and parsed back in a useMemo keyed on that string — which deep-unwraps the snapshot proxies (arrays included, e.g. a ChoicePicker answer) AND gives the replay memo a stable identity. FIX-3 (missing root): useA2uiSurface now reports `missingRoot` when any created surface has no `root` in its componentsModel (checking the processed model, not the raw envelopes, also covers an agent that names its root differently); ChatA2uiBlock renders A2uiFallback for it, except while `message.inProgress` (mid-stream), where it renders nothing rather than flashing the notice. A2uiErrorBoundary gained an optional `resetKey` prop plus componentDidUpdate, so a boundary latched on an intermediate streaming state clears when the envelopes change; ChatA2uiBlock passes `${surfaceIds}:${envelopes.length}`. FIX-4 (multi-surface): envelopes.ts exports `findCreatedSurfaceIds()` (all createSurface ids, ordered, de-duplicated) replacing the first-match-only `findCreatedSurfaceId`; ChatA2uiBlock builds a per-surface answer map (surfaceId -> {turnIndex, item}) from the history, and prefill, submitted-action marker, read-only state and `replaceHistoryIndex` are all resolved per surface. useA2uiSurface's third argument became `prefillDataModels?: Record<surfaceId, A2uiDataModel>` and replays one updateDataModel per ANSWERED surface only, so an unanswered sibling keeps its server defaults. Each surface now renders in its own <fieldset> + A2uiSubmittedActionProvider, so one answered surface can be read-only while its sibling stays answerable. FIX-5 (double submit / fire-and-forget): handleAction is async, guarded by a synchronous `inFlightRef` latch (set before the first await, cleared in `finally`) plus an `isSubmitting` state that feeds isSurfaceActive and the fieldset; the submitA2uiAction promise is awaited and its rejection caught. On the store side submitA2uiAction wraps createChatGeneration in try/catch and reports failures raised BEFORE the optimistic chip exists (e.g. the assistant lookup) through the existing `_handleGenerationStreamError` + toaster.error — the post-chip path stays with `_handleRequestError`, whose rollback logic is not duplicated. FIX-6 (invalid submit): new exported `isSurfaceValid(surface)` in useA2uiSurface.ts walks the surface's componentsModel, evaluates every component's `checks` rules against a root DataContext (resolveDynamicValue, non-reactive/peek — no subscription leak) and returns false on the first failing rule; rules whose condition references a relative path (list-item scope, unevaluatable at root) or that throw are skipped so they can never trap the user. handleAction refuses to submit an invalid surface.

notes_for_next_tasks: (1) FIX-6 is only enforced in handleAction — the Button's own `disabled={props.isValid === false}` in src/a2ui/registry.tsx (owned by the parallel agent) still reacts only to checks declared ON the button, so an invalid form shows an enabled button that does nothing when clicked; wiring the aggregated validity into the button's disabled state needs a registry-side change (e.g. reading surface validity from context). (2) The FIX-6 guard blocks EVERY action of an invalid surface, including non-submit-like buttons (Cancel/Back) — A2UI has no way to distinguish them; if a surface with a required field plus a Decline button appears, the user would be trapped and the guard must become action-scoped. (3) isSurfaceValid evaluates checks at the surface root and deliberately skips conditions using relative paths (list-item scope) — a form whose validation lives inside a List is not enforced. (4) The multi-surface path (FIX-4) has unit coverage only; the backend currently emits one surface per turn, so a browser check is still worth doing if that changes. (5) `isSubmitting` stays true for the whole generation (the submit promise resolves when the stream ends), which overlaps with the existing isChatBusy lock — no behavioural difference observed, but worth knowing when reading the code.
